messages:
Sam (AE): Kicking off the Rivermark POC thread. Need to align on the compat approach (façade) and immediate blockers. Can we do a 90-min workshop Wed 10am PT? @Priya @Alex :calendar:
Priya (SE): Wed 10am works for me. I need their sample prompts, expected outputs, and any custom headers/session semantics. Also curious about their burst profile vs steady QPS.
Ravi (Rivermark-CTO): Wed 10 is fine. We'll drop a prompt bundle + a short video of client behavior. Main concern: we rely on session_id affinity + streaming partial tokens; parity here is critical for UX.
Sam (AE): Noted. Also pricing sensitivity on their side — they want a blended per-1M-token rate + reserved pool for peak windows. We'll need cost scenarios.
Priya (SE): On the technical side: we can provide a compat façade that maps their API to our runtime. Streaming is supported (chunked responses). Key tests: session handshake, prefix/KV cache behavior, and tokenizer differences that cause token deltas.
Alex (SRE): Staging network: we'll allocate 10.120.5.0/24 for them. Please give us CIDR allowlist for their egress. Provisioning Dedicated GPU pools ~3 weeks after signed commit FYI.
Jordan (PM): I'll produce a mapping doc for the workshop: prompt -> template mapping, expected delta categories (tokenization, formatting, hallucination), and a small response-normalization shim to try during the session.
Priya (SE): Action items I see: 1) Rivermark to upload top 50 prompt pairs + 50 canonical expected outputs 2) We run an initial parity pass and surface the top 10 deltas 3) Deliver a POC playbook with mitigation options (prompt rewrite, canonicalizer, fallback model routing).
SecurityBot: Heads up — Rivermark requested SOC2 artifacts and encryption-in-transit docs. Uploading our standard security questionnaire form: https://redwood.internal/sec/questionnaire/2026/rivermark (private link) :lock:
Ravi (Rivermark-CTO): We'll need KMS integration inside a VPC and HSM options. Also data residency requirements: EU region mandatory for a subset of traffic.
Priya (SE): Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and HSM (BYOK flow). EU region available. I'll flag this in the SOW and loop in legal for DPA. Marta (security lead) will be the contact.
Sam (AE): Pricing ask from sales: can we provide 20% off in year one for a 12-mo reserved capacity commit? Also need clarity on per-token billing when fallback to smaller models happens.
Jordan (PM): Pricing structure we usually propose: base reserved + overage. For this deal we can propose a blended per-token rate with reserved throughput. Priya — can you estimate token footprint from their sample set?
Priya (SE): Quick rough calc: 50 prompt pairs -> avg prompt 350 tokens, avg response 180 tokens -> ~26k tokens per run. If they run 10k sessions/day that's ~260M tokens/day. I'll draft hosted vs dedicated vs private cost scenarios with quantization options and expected unit economics.
Alex (SRE): Connectivity smoke test for their infra (staging):

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Session-Id: 12345" \
  https://staging.redwood-infer.net/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-compat-v1","input":"hello"}'

Expect streaming (chunked) responses; content-length will be omitted. If they see long tails, check KV cache TTL mismatch.
Priya (SE): Note on token accounting: tokenizer mismatch can create systematic token deltas. Recommend a tiny tokenizer-normalization step in the façade (pre-tokenize + canonical whitespace) to reduce noise before measuring parity.
Sam (AE): Next steps: Rivermark to post samples + security contact; we'll run a pre-workshop parity run and share a short report; workshop Wed 10am PT — I'll send the calendar invite and agenda.
Ravi (Rivermark-CTO): Sending sample bundle and Marta (marta@rivermark.com) as security lead. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Priya (SE): Received — I'll spin up the parity harness and a minimal compat façade prototype that maps GatekeeperAPI session semantics to our runtime for the workshop demo.
Jordan (PM): I'll prepare a decision-ready cost comparison table (hosted / dedicated / private), include latency SLOs, and outline fallback policies (model variants + routing). See you all Wed :thumbsup:
